newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil traders can't confirm China resold soymeal.
newsitem.headline: Brazil traders can't confirm China resold soymeal.

text.p: Brazil traders said they had heard talk that China resold up to 400,000 tonnes of South American soymeal but they had no confirmation as yet.
"Everybody is talking about it but nobody has any confirmation," said one trader. "They're talking about 400,000 tonnes of wash-out."
Traders said they did not know how much of this would be Brazilian soymeal.
"It makes sense from a business point of view that they actually might do it. The Chinese have been known to do it before so it wouldn't be very surprising," the trader said.
Another trader said the rumors started on Feb 19 and some people were saying 10,000 tonnes of soymeal had already been resold. "They say the Chinese are making a $45 profit," he said.
But it was impossible for China to resell soymeal to Brazil if it had already been registered for export, the trader added.
"It seems more likely one of the big multinationals is acting as middleman. If anyone is buying it back it is probably them," he said.

"I talked to people here and no one has heard anything about it," he added. "But they wouldn't necessarily know. If the product hasn't been shipped they would only know where the product is going once the vessel has been nominated."
Some traders suggested that if the product has not yet been shipped, it could be that the company which sold it is having trouble loading it.
Paranagua port started loading the 1996/97 soybean harvest this week but traders said there was not enough produce in stock to cover existing spot commitments.
